parsed.explanation: The operative regime is a national Penal Code criminalising same-sex conduct and marriage, with penalties up to eight years and lashes, extended to all persons. No trans-specific offence, document, facility, custody or care rule is documented. No anti-discrimination protection exists, official posture is restrictive, and a UN agency records hate crimes against people perceived as homosexual or transgender. Enforcement of the same-sex law is documented only in 2015, so it is a secondary lever rather than a proven campaign against gender-nonconforming visitors. Resort tolerance is travel guidance, not a legal carve-out; the Penal Code's non-application there is unresolved. A trans visitor is not criminalised for identity alone, but if outed faces social stigma, possible violence and no realistic recourse. This places the jurisdiction in the elevated-risk band, below active state trans-targeting cases but above jurisdictions with functioning protections.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific border, document or screening rule is documented; the record does not state how a trans person's gender is classified under the sex-based Penal Code or whether foreign markers are recognised.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry treatment is unresolved; resort guidance is not a legal carve-out.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Same-sex conduct is criminalised with penalties up to eight years and lashes; one 2015 arrest of two men in a private home is documented, with no later instance. No trans-specific custody or placement rule is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If arrested, classification under sex-based law and custody placement are unresolved; no anti-discrimination recourse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No trans-specific facility rule is documented; resorts are described as LGBTQ-welcoming in travel guidance, but no source establishes the Penal Code does not apply there.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private resort practice only; not an enforceable legal protection.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Tourist enclaves may buffer social friction, but no legal safe haven is established.

care_services.exposure: No trans-specific care restriction is documented; no anti-discrimination law covers gender identity.
care_services.interaction: Stigma or service denial is possible without recourse, but no documented rule reaches visitors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State rejected 60 UPR recommendations including LGBT matters, rejected UN SOGI resolutions, and the president's office said asylum claimants would face prosecution on return; no GI/SO anti-discrimination law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official hostility frames LGBT conduct as against Islamic faith and the Constitution, raising risk if outed.

minors_guardians.exposure: No minor-specific trans rule is documented; the same general criminal and social climate applies.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult travelling with a minor faces no additional documented state measure, but no protection if outed.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: A UN agency reports people perceived as homosexual or transgender were targets of hate crimes and other violations; a 2013 stabbing of a gay blogger is documented; local advocates warned tourists could face similar threats. No trans-specific figures are given.
street_violence_police_response.protection: A 2020 foreign report found no officials complicit, but stigma likely discouraged reporting.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse is thin; police protection for trans victims is not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination protection or effective remedy is documented; UPR recommendations were not accepted; resort legal status and trans classification under sex-based law are unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Complaints are unlikely to yield protection; unresolved questions resolve toward the hostile structural signals.

anchor_checks.comparison: Ostravia documents prison housing by birth sex, a cross-dressing offence and frequent assaults, with solitary used as protection. The present dossier has no trans-specific custody rule, no cross-dressing offence and no documented pattern of assaults on trans detainees, so it sits above 0.25-C, though the same-sex law and hostile climate keep it well below safe.

Karthovia documents routine police stops of trans visitors, passport confiscation, compelled interviews and fines, with courts deferring to police. The present dossier records no such pattern against trans visitors; its only enforcement is a 2015 same-sex arrest. That makes it safer than 0.35-B, but official hostility and no recourse keep it in the elevated band.

Kestrel Isles documents trans-specific border secondary screening, private interviews, refused admission and slow appeals. The present dossier has no documented trans-specific border screening or denial, but it has a criminal same-sex law, no anti-discrimination protection and recorded anti-LGBT hate crimes. The direct border exposure is lower, while the social-legal climate is worse, placing it below 0.55-B.

Meridia permits entry on passports matching presentation, trains border officers, and provides tribunal appeals and compensation for unlawful detention. The present dossier documents no such protections, no anti-discrimination law and a restrictive official posture, so it is far below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is national: the Penal Code criminalises same-sex conduct and marriage, with penalties up to eight years and lashes, and the record documents no trans-specific offence, document, facility, custody or care rule. Tourist-island tolerance is travel guidance, not an enforceable carve-out, and the Penal Code's non-application there is unresolved. No anti-discrimination protection exists; official posture is restrictive; a UN agency records hate crimes against people perceived as homosexual or transgender. Enforcement of the same-sex law is documented only in 2015, so it is a secondary lever rather than a proven campaign against gender-nonconforming visitors. A trans visitor is not criminalised for identity alone, but if outed faces social stigma, possible violence and no realistic recourse. The absence of trans-specific data in a hostile structural setting resolves toward elevated risk, not neutrality.
